latest.title: Why IAM Alone Isn't Enough for AI Agents: Building Runtime Governance on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
latest.description: A production case study on securing AI agents when the model itself can be turned against you. IAM scopes identity but not intent so a prompt-injected agent can act within its permissions. This walks through building the missing layer on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore: deterministic enforcement at the tool boundary, stateful cross-call budgets, task-intent authorization, machine-speed containment, and the fail-closed and audit trade-offs that come with it.

latest.title: Workflow-Level SLOs for AI Agents on AWS Implementing the Compounding Reliability Math with Step Functions, CloudWatch, and the agentsre Framework
latest.description:
The math published this week changed how I think about AI agent architecture on AWS.
At 95% per-step accuracy, a 10-step agent workflow succeeds only 60% of the time. At 20 steps, 36%. And in reality steps aren't independent an incorrect output at step 2 feeds into step 3, which breaks everything else. Compounding is worse in practice than the raw multiplication suggests.
